evidence.s1_ci: Strengths: ci.yml (step1.patch 36-76) runs on `pull_request` and runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in site/. All three scripts exist in app/site/package.json:15-16, and `build` runs svelte-check. pages.yml triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` plus workflow_dispatch. Its top-level permissions are `contents: read`, and only the deploy job gets `pages: write` and `id-token: write`. No workflow uses `pull_request_target`. pr-title.yml passes the title through `env:`, not by inline interpolation. Failures: every action is pinned to a major tag, not a commit SHA. This applies to actions/checkout@v7, setup-node@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5, deploy-pages@v5 and googleapis/release-please-action@v5 (step1.patch 59, 61, 128, 130, 147, 216, 232). release.yml:221 uses `secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, a secret beyond GITHUB_TOKEN, and CONTRIBUTING.md:372 asks maintainers to create it. release.yml also sets `contents/pull-requests/issues: write` for the whole workflow, so the data-archive job inherits PR and issues write that it does not need.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 380-470) covers install (`cd site && npm ci`), develop (`npm run dev`), test (`npm test`), build and preview, other scripts, a contribution section, CI and releases, and the license (MIT, matching app/LICENSE). Every command shown exists in site/package.json:9-17. PAGES_BASE is real: vite.config.ts:11 reads it. Data contribution is only a link to CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-data. That section is thorough: paths, families, sources, the tests to run, fixtures. But the README itself carries no data instructions.
evidence.s1_release: The version source is .release-please-manifest.json (0.1.0), copied to version.txt and site/package.json via extra-files (release-please-config.json). All three hold 0.1.0. Releases are made by release-please on main: merging its PR creates the v<version> tag and the GitHub release, and the data archive is attached (release.yml). CHANGELOG.md states its format, release-please writes it, and the sections match changelog-sections in the config. Dependabot covers npm in /site (the only package.json) and GitHub Actions, with `chore(deps)` and `ci(deps)` prefixes that fit the convention. Conventional Commits 1.0.0 is stated in CONTRIBUTING.md:293-319, with a SemVer pre-1.0 bump rule. All nine commits in commits.txt follow it (ci:, build:, build(deps):, docs:, feat(site):, fix(site):).
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: router.ts:34-44 parses `#/compare/<a>/<b>` from location.hash, so a reload works. Drawing: Compare.svelte draws one `path` per outline in an `svg role=img`, with aria-label `compare.profiles` = 'Profiles of {a} and {b}'. Both outlines share one viewport from viewportFor([first, second]) with z=0 at the head face. Shotshells return null, and a message is shown. Table: the caption is `Dimensions ({unit})`. Headers are Symbol, name A, name B and Difference, and Difference is b - a. Rows come from the cartridge part only, numbers only, with no FIELD_UNITS entry, no Tol fields, and FIELD_LABELS symbols (compare.ts dimensionsOf). Units use unitSystem(), formatValue for metric and displayNumber in inches for imperial. The detail page has a Label 'Compare with', a NativeSelect of the other cartridges sorted by name, and a 'Compare' submit button that sets href.compare(key, picked). German strings are in the de table. Tests were added, and the commit is feat(site). No requirement unmet.
evidence.s2_correctness: dimensionsOf follows GROUP_ORDER and orderedFields, skips arrays (shot repeating groups), non-numbers and FIELD_UNITS fields (alpha, delta, beta, Pmax…), and maps eMin to 'e min' and deltaL to 'delta L'. Metric differences are cut to 12 significant digits to avoid float noise such as 15.369999999999997. That matches what displayNumber does for imperial (units.ts:12-13) and adds no real rounding. Imperial divides by 25.4 through displayNumber, and the caption unit is defaultUnit('length'), i.e. 'in'. Both outlines use one Viewport, so they share scale, the axis at y = rMax + margin and the head face at x = margin*scale. fullSectionPath mirrors each profile about the common axis. A malformed or encoded key falls back to the list view, and an unknown key shows load()'s error message.
evidence.s2_fit: Reuses @lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), @lib/shapes2d/case (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), @lib/geom/svg (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), site/src/lib/units.ts, and the PageHeader, NativeSelect, Label and ShadcnButton components. The logic is a framework-free site/src/lib/compare.ts with its test beside it, following the router.ts and metadata.ts patterns. The route is wired into App.svelte chunks, SiteNavigation and metadata. Minor: Compare.svelte's table CSS repeats GroupTable.svelte:226-248 instead of sharing it. compare.test.ts imports `../../../lib/testing/fixtures` by relative path. The symbol cell carries class `num` even though it holds text.
evidence.s2_tests: compare.test.ts covers: field filtering (Tol, FIELD_UNITS, angles, strings, null), label mapping and order, cartridge-only reading, skipping repeating groups, shared rows on synthetic and real 308 Win/300 Win Mag records, metric and imperial formatting, the B−A sign, the drawing geometry (head face at min x, common scale and axis, symmetry, closed path), and null for shotshells. router.test.ts covers the route round-trip, encoding and malformed hashes. Missing: nothing checks the rendered page, such as the SVG accessible name, table headers or caption, or the Compare-with select and button. The repo has no component-test setup, so this is a moderate gap.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: sharedDimensions became comparedDimensions (step3.patch 111-139). It returns every symbol from either record, with null where a record lacks it, and puts B-only symbols after the last matched symbol to keep the sheet order. formatLength and formatDifference return '' for null, so those cells are empty. Tests assert delta L (only 308 Win. publishes it) and R3 (only 300 Win. Mag. publishes it) on the real records, plus the exact order on synthetic records. Style: cells and headers of the three value columns get class `value` with `text-align: right`, and Symbol stays left. Step 2 CSS already right-aligned those columns, so this change only refactors the rule. Side effects: the headers gain class `num`, which switches them to a monospace font (app.css:53). The lede and noShared texts in EN and DE were reworded to match the new behaviour.
evidence.cross_step: Steps 2 and 3 are committed as `feat(site): add cartridge comparison view` and two `fix(site): …` commits, all in the stated convention. Under the stated release-please strategy, CHANGELOG.md, version.txt and the manifest are generated and must not be edited by hand (CONTRIBUTING.md:327-336), so leaving them untouched is correct. The new code is typed and uses existing APIs (unitSystem, load, href, NativeSelect props), and the tests target existing fixtures. I did not run them, but nothing in the code suggests npm test or svelte-check would fail.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 / CI criteria: actions are pinned to major tags (@v5–@v7), not full commit SHAs
Step 1 / CI criteria: release.yml uses a secret beyond GITHUB_TOKEN (RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN), and CONTRIBUTING asks maintainers to create it
strengths: The compare feature reuses the repository's own modules: core field order, labels, units and formatValue; shapes2d adaptMetallic and caseOuterProfile; geom viewportFor and fullSectionPath on one shared viewport. Its logic sits in a framework-free, well-tested site/src/lib/compare.ts.

The release setup is consistent: the release-please manifest, version.txt and site/package.json all hold 0.1.0; the changelog format is stated; Dependabot prefixes fit Conventional Commits; and every commit follows the convention.

The step 3 bug fix is correct and tested against the real records (delta L only in 308 Win., R3 only in 300 Win. Mag.). Rows keep the sheet order, and the cells a cartridge does not publish, plus their Difference, are empty.
issues: Every GitHub Action is referenced by a mutable major tag (actions/checkout@v7, deploy-pages@v5, release-please-action@v5, …), not a full commit SHA. This is a supply-chain risk for a repo that accepts outside PRs.

release.yml relies on an extra secret, `secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which CONTRIBUTING tells maintainers to create. Its write permissions (contents, pull-requests, issues) are set for the whole workflow, so the data-archive job inherits more than it needs.

There are no rendered-page tests for the SVG accessible name, the table headers and caption, or the Compare-with select. The table CSS repeats GroupTable's, and the step 3 alignment change also switched the headers to monospace.
review.verdict: The compare feature and the step 3 fix are correct, well tested and built on the repository's own modules, and the versioning, changelog and commit convention are coherent and followed across all steps. The CI setup falls short of the security requirements: actions are not pinned to commit SHAs and the release workflow depends on an extra secret, so I would require those fixes before merging.
